messages:
alex: Heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate jumped after this morning's canary of the token limiter + prefetch tweaks. Numbers from the dashboard: p95 180ms -> 250ms, p99 620ms -> 840ms. Canary id: canary-2026-03-17-11. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

mira: Saw the spike. It lines up with the token-limiter slope change (0.6 -> 0.3) and prefetch TTL reduction. Charts: https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-17/canary (looks like microbatch count went up).

sam: Reproduced locally with synthetic seq=64 workload. Microbatch distribution shifted to many 1-2 request microbatches. Profiling output shows increased wakeups and more time in the batcher queue. Snippet from perf flame:```
batcher_poll() +45ms
  assemble_microbatch() +30ms
    kernel_select() +6ms
      prepare_kv_prefetch() +12ms
prefetch_worker() +38ms
```

oliver: We also pushed a kernel-selector tweak yesterday to prefer fused matmul for seq>=128. For seq<128 the selector now often picks the generic path which seems to have worse prefetch behavior. Might be an interaction: token limiter causing smaller batches -> more calls into the generic kernel.

alex: Quick logs from a problematic instance (canary):
```
route=/v1/generate tid=0x47 kv_hit=0.78 -> 0.32 microbatch_count_p95=3 -> 9 p95=180->250ms
canary=canary-2026-03-17-11 token_limiter.slope=0.3
```

perf-bot: Automated check: microbatch_count_p95 increased by 210% on route /v1/generate during canary window. Latency SLA breach flag set for canary-id canary-2026-03-17-11. (link: https://alerts.internal/alert/9876)

mira: Two-pronged short-term plan: 1) revert token-limiter slope to 0.6 for the canary group, 2) bump prefetch TTL back to 200ms so KV warmups aren't starving. Quick test before rollback: increase token_budget_target for high-tier routes by +30%.

sam: Also propose a small kernel-affinity guard: in kernel-selector, if median_seq < 96 and predicted_batch_size < 8, prefer the prefetch-friendly generic kernel until we adjust prefetch sizing. Pseudoconfig: ```
{
  "token_limiter": { "slope": 0.6 },
  "batcher_queue_policy": { "max_wait_ms": 6, "min_batch_tokens": 64 },
  "kernel_selector": { "force_generic_if_small_batch": true }
}
```

alex: Rolling a canary patch that reverts token_limiter.slope + applies kernel-affinity guard to 10% of instances in region-us-east-1. Starting now, will monitor p95 and kv_hit. infra-bot, kick the deploy? :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy started: deploy/2026-03-17/revert-slope-kernel-guard -> canary group (10%). Watch: https://deploys.internal/2026-03-17/5678

oliver: Good. Also adding a regression test to the perf harness: assert microbatch_count_p95 doesn't increase >10% vs baseline for the route under seq distribution X (we keep getting surprised by microbatch regressions). I'll open a PR for harness + alert rule.

alex: After 5 minutes canary metrics look promising: p95 back to ~185ms, kv_hit up to ~0.71. I'll hold for 15 more minutes and then promote.

mira: Nice. Post-mortem action items: 1) add unit to kernel-selector that reasons about prefetch window and microbatch size, 2) add canary metric for microbatch_count_p95 so we catch this earlier, 3) run a small sweep of token-limiter slopes in perf lab to map out stability region.

sam: Also add a synthetic test that varies seq lengths (16/32/64/128) and checks kernel path choices + kv_hit behaviour. That should have caught the interaction.

perf-bot: Canary health check summary (10m window): p95 deviation -2.7% vs baseline, microbatch_count_p95 -15%, kv_hit +12%. Canary flagged as healthy.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees blips, ping this thread. We'll file a short RFC for kernel-selector + prefetch policy changes to avoid future surprises. :white_check_mark:
